transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Hassan, thank you for coming back in. I wanted to sit down and talk with you about why you're back in the emergency department and what happened with your discharge yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can imagine why I'm here. My wound is leaking and I can't walk straight. I just want to know why I was kicked out so early.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've looked at your chart and the protocol. The surgical guidelines stated you needed to stay for a specific window of observation, but you were discharged six hours before that window closed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Six hours. So I was just a number on a checklist that someone missed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure in the discharge timing process. The medical team didn't adhere to the post-op timeline.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You know, this isn't the first time. Every time I come to this hospital, something "fails." I'm tired of being the one who pays for these failures with my own body.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how exhausted you are with this. It sounds like you're feeling completely worn out by having to deal with these kinds of mistakes repeatedly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am. I'm more than worn out. I'm cynical. I expected this. Why should I believe anything you say now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand why you'd feel that way. It's frustrating to feel like you can't trust the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Did anyone actually look at me before I left, or did they just see a bed that needed to be cleared?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The clinical review happened, but the timing of the release was incorrect. The protocol was bypassed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Bypassed. That's a very clean word for it. Who did it? Who decided I was good to go?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The discharge order was processed prematurely by the team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're not telling me who did it. You're telling me it "was processed."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a team error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That doesn't help me. My leg is throbbing and I had to drive back here in pain. Do you even care that I'm back here?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I do. It is not acceptable that you are back in this bed today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? Do I just sit here and wait for another "process" to fail?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right now, the immediate priority is the wound. I've already paged the attending surgeon. He is coming to see you within the next thirty minutes to assess the closure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Once he assesses you, we are going to keep you for another twenty-four hours of observation to make sure the complication is stable. I will personally check your vitals and the dressing every four hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'll believe that when I see it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. While we wait for the surgeon, I want you to keep your leg elevated exactly as it is now, and please press the call button immediately if you feel any new numbness.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I know how to be a patient. I've had plenty of practice.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you have. I'll be back in a few minutes to check on you before the surgeon arrives.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient, remains regulated despite significant pushback, and allows the patient to express frustration without rushing.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn, but there were no comprehension checks performed throughout the transcript.

A.justification: No direct apology language such as 'I'm sorry' or 'I apologize' was used, and responsibility was framed passively as a 'team error' or 'failure in the process'.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions ('exhausted', 'worn out', 'frustrating') and engaged with the patient's emotional bids regarding trust and cynicism.

T.justification: The resident provided specific steps (surgeon visit, 24-hour observation), timelines (30 minutes, every 4 hours), a patient role (elevate leg, press call button), and a prevention measure (personal vitals checks).
